The system operates under a dual-layered logic: first, the URL encoding mechanism establishes a persistent session state through structured identifiers, enabling tracking of customer actions across pages. Second, the dynamic cart state machine reflects real-time interaction with product listings, updating internal representations upon user input. These mechanisms interlock to form a coherent model of user intent and commerce flow. The core duality lies in the static nature of session identifiers versus the fluidity of cart contents. Failure modes emerge from inconsistent state propagation—such as when a product is added but not reflected in the cart due to server lag—or when referral credits are miscalculated due to missing or corrupted associate identifiers. The system’s resilience depends on maintaining consistency between client-side cookies, server-side sessions, and database entries.
